title: Machine Learning
headline: Turn data into decisions you can explain.
intro: Build a complete machine-learning workflow: frame a question, prepare data, train a useful baseline, evaluate honestly and deliver a small prediction service.
audience: College learners, graduates and experienced developers
bridge: One course, two entry points. New learners start with a Python, data and statistics bridge. Experienced developers can demonstrate readiness and focus on deeper experiments, reproducibility and service integration.
scope: This is a dedicated machine-learning program. Classical supervised and unsupervised learning form the core; neural networks are introduced after sound evaluation habits. It is distinct from the generative-AI internship.
paths: Practise Python functions, tables, visualisation and essential probability before the modelling labs.
Use the readiness exercise to identify gaps, then extend experiments with stronger validation and API delivery.

modules.title: Python, data & statistical thinking
modules.summary: Build the language and reasoning needed to work with data.
topics: Missing values, outliers and exploratory questions
tools: Jupyter + Git — explain and version experiments
modules.practice: Explore an openly licensed or synthetic dataset. Produce a short data-quality report and distinguish an observation from a causal claim.
deliverables: A data dictionary and quality report
criteria: The notebook runs in a fresh environment
Plots label units and sample sizes
Limitations and missing data are visible

modules.title: Problem framing & reliable datasets
modules.summary: Define the prediction target and protect evaluation from leakage.
topics: Feature availability at prediction time and preprocessing
tools: scikit-learn Pipeline + ColumnTransformer — fit preprocessing on training data
modules.practice: Create a prediction contract for a synthetic service dataset. Build a split strategy and deliberately expose a leaked feature before removing it.
criteria: Test data remains untouched during model selection
Split choice matches the intended use
Unavailable-at-inference features are excluded

modules.title: Feature engineering & reproducible pipelines
modules.summary: Make the same transformations work reliably during training and prediction.
topics: Categorical encoding, scaling and skewed distributions
tools: ColumnTransformer and Pipeline — join transformations with estimators
pytest — test feature contracts and unseen-category behaviour
modules.practice: Build a reusable preprocessing pipeline for mixed numerical and categorical data. Introduce an unseen category and missing field, then document the intended prediction-time behaviour.
deliverables: Tests for missing and unfamiliar inputs
criteria: Fit learned transformations only on training folds
Explain what each feature means at prediction time
Keep validation data out of feature selection

modules.title: Supervised learning & useful baselines
modules.summary: Compare models against a baseline before chasing complexity.
tools: scikit-learn — dummy, linear and tree models
modules.practice: Compare a dummy baseline, a linear model and a tree ensemble. Explain where a more complex model improves results and where it does not.
criteria: All candidates use the same validation protocol
Metrics match the problem and class balance
Training scores are not presented as deployment evidence

modules.title: Regression, classification & model comparison
modules.summary: Understand which model family is useful, and why its errors differ.
topics: Linear and logistic regression, regularisation and decision boundaries
Decision trees, random forests and gradient boosting
Nearest neighbours and support-vector machines as comparison models
Probability estimates, thresholds and the cost of different errors
tools: DummyRegressor and DummyClassifier — establish simple baselines
Matplotlib — inspect residuals, learning curves and confusion matrices
modules.practice: Compare a linear model, a tree ensemble and a dummy baseline on the same fixed split. Explain a case where the most complex model is not the most useful choice.
deliverables: Comparison table with identical evaluation conditions
A model-choice note with operational constraints
criteria: Use the same data split and metric definitions
Separate hyperparameter selection from final test evaluation
Explain errors and resource costs as well as headline scores

modules.title: Evaluation, tuning & explanation
modules.summary: Explain model performance, uncertainty and important failure cases.
topics: Precision, recall, F1, ROC/PR curves and regression errors
tools: scikit-learn — validation, metrics and permutation importance
modules.practice: Choose a threshold for a sample support-triage model. Show the tradeoff between missed urgent cases and unnecessary reviews, then evaluate once on held-out data.
criteria: Validation and final-test results are distinguished
Error slices include minority groups or rare cases where relevant
Explanations do not imply causation

modules.title: Time-aware prediction & forecasting
modules.summary: Respect the order in which information becomes available.
topics: Forecast horizons and seasonal or lag features
Delayed labels, missing periods and changing patterns
Prediction intervals as an introductory uncertainty topic
tools: pandas datetime tools — align time-indexed observations
scikit-learn — compare lag-feature regression against a baseline
modules.practice: Forecast a sample daily demand series. Hold out the latest period, construct features using past data only and compare performance across busy and quiet intervals.
deliverables: Forecast notebook and chronological split diagram
Limitations note for sparse history and unexpected events
criteria: Never use future observations to construct past features
Evaluate on the horizon the proposed user needs
Avoid presenting a forecast as a certain business outcome

modules.title: Patterns, text & neural-network foundations
modules.summary: Explore learning beyond labelled tabular predictions.
topics: Neural-network concepts, overfitting and compute budgets
tools: scikit-learn — clustering, PCA and text pipelines
PyTorch — a small introductory neural-network exercise
modules.practice: Group synthetic service requests and compare a text classifier with a simple neural baseline on a small approved dataset. Keep conclusions proportional to the evidence.
criteria: Clusters are reviewed rather than treated as ground truth
Text preprocessing respects data splits
Compute and overfitting controls are recorded

modules.title: Prediction services & model lifecycle
modules.summary: Make the experiment usable by another developer.
topics: Saving preprocessing and model artifacts together
Typed inference requests and invalid-input handling
modules.practice: Package the chosen model behind a small API and optional UI. Rehearse a schema change, an invalid request and a shifted sample dataset.
criteria: The full transformation pipeline is reproduced at inference
Untrusted model artifacts are not loaded
Drift prompts investigation rather than automatic blind retraining

modules.title: Monitoring, responsible use & capstone review
modules.summary: Show when a model is useful, when it should defer and when it needs review.
topics: Data drift versus changes in predictive performance
Subgroup error analysis and limitations of small samples
Human review, inappropriate uses and sensitive data minimisation
Model cards, reproducibility and retraining approval
tools: pandas — compare input distributions and labelled outcomes
Python monitoring scripts — generate a small review report
Git and a model-card template — version assumptions and intended use
modules.practice: Simulate a change in input distribution and a rise in error once labels arrive. Prepare a review recommendation and a human fallback; do not automate retraining simply because a drift score changed.
deliverables: Model card with intended use and exclusions
Capstone review package and reproducibility instructions
criteria: Distinguish a drift signal from evidence of model failure
State sample-size limitations when comparing groups
Document who decides whether to retain, revise or retire the model

projects.title: Service-demand prediction
projects.problem: An operations team needs a better estimate of demand than last-period averages.
projects.practice: Build and compare a simple forecasting-style tabular regression workflow using time-appropriate features. Use a chronological holdout when observations are time-dependent. Compare a naive forecast with feature-based regression, inspect unusually high and low demand separately, and explain the effect of unavailable or delayed inputs. End with a recommendation that connects the error measure to the proposed planning task.
failures: A changed process invalidates old patterns

projects.title: Support-request triage
projects.problem: A team wants suggested categories and urgency flags while retaining human review.
projects.practice: Build a text classifier and explain threshold, class imbalance and uncertain predictions. Create a small labelled sample with explicit categories and a held-out evaluation set. Compare a simple text baseline with another justified model. Inspect confused categories, document when to send a request to human review and show what happens to a request outside the known topics.
failures: Personal information appears in raw text

projects.title: An evaluated prediction API
projects.problem: A useful notebook needs a reliable interface before another application can use it.
projects.practice: Integrate the chosen model with a small service, input checks and reproducible setup. Package preprocessing and prediction together so the service applies the same transformations used during training. Validate inputs, test missing and unknown values and return an explicit error for unsupported requests. Reproduce the saved model result, then prepare a release note and a monitoring review for changing inputs.

preparation: Present the problem, split, baseline, metric and error cases in a concise technical walkthrough. Walk through the data split, baseline, feature availability and metric choice before showing a result. Use one failed experiment to explain what you learned and what you changed.

Reason through bias/variance, leakage, imbalance, feature availability and metric selection with examples. Practise bias–variance tradeoffs, regularisation, cross-validation, threshold selection and leakage detection. Explain your answer with a small dataset or diagram, then discuss how the answer changes for time-dependent data.

Prepare notebooks, a model card, an API demonstration and a README another developer can follow. Include a dataset description, pinned environment, training command, evaluation report and model card. A reviewer should be able to reproduce a representative result without private credentials.

Explain limitations, privacy boundaries, review needs and the cost of an incorrect prediction. Identify an inappropriate use of your model, a weakly represented data segment and a fallback for unsupported input. Explain uncertainty without implying that a score makes the application safe for every use.
curriculumTitle: Machine Learning curriculum: from data to dependable predictions.
curriculumIntro: Explore ten modules: data preparation, feature pipelines, regression, classification, model comparison, evaluation, time-aware prediction, neural foundations and delivery.
